statement: Student proposal: because a hash cannot be reversed (two different emails can collide), the hash must be stored in the users table.
detail: The teacher did not adopt this reason. He answered that you can instead apply the hash function in the where clause (where hash(email) = the given hash). The hash column was added later for a different reason: so it can be indexed and the lookup avoids a full table scan.
speaker: student (proposal)
verbatim: So we have to have a hash stored because in it, we cannot go in a reverse way from email.

statement: The origin-side on-demand transformation design (read the image from S3, transform it with ImageMagick, return it) assumes the CDN does not provide image transformation; if you are building your own CDN, this is exactly how you would implement that feature.
detail: Said right after explaining that the request cannot be made async; it frames the whole on-demand design as what a CDN provider itself does internally.
speaker: teacher
verbatim: So if you are building your own CDN, this is exactly how you do it.
